I remember being able to tap rotary phones in phone boxes to get free calls. All you had to do was tap the receiver to make whatever number you needed to dial add up to 10. For example if you needed to dial 1 then you would tap the receiver 9 times, to dial 9 you would tap once. Zero was the only exception, you simply dial zero. It worked with rotary phones in the home too but there was no point of course.

As a side story. One day I was having trouble with my touch tone land line. I could hear the person at the other end but they couldn't hear me. So I rang faults and when the service man answered I tapped out S.O.S on the phone pad until he realized and said "S.O.S?" to which I responded with a single tone to establish 1 tone = "yes" that allowed us to communicate enough for him to log the fault and set about fixing it.

I always had a safety pin on me for the touch tone phone booths. If you held a piece of metal into the middle hole of the microphone part of the handset, and touched it to the metal part where you hung up the handset after a call, the phone thought a quarter was put in and you could dial a local number for free.
You not only used to have to remember telephone numbers, but you had to remember facts and information too.

They had names for the prefixes like VIctor, MElrose, WIndsor. The first 2 characters equated to numbers EX: 84, 63, 94 from the previous names. So Victor 2-1111 was dialed as 842-1111.
